sop_modules.name: Porch Floor RP — Mobilization & Furniture Staging
sop_modules.description: Crew mobilization, equipment staging, and furniture/obstacle removal from porch surface. Ground-level work — no scaffold.

tasks.name: Crew Mobilization & Equipment Staging
tasks.description: Load and transport RP-specific equipment: roller frames, brushes, scrapers, chemical deglosser, sandpaper, anti-slip aggregate, primer and porch enamel. Stage at work area.

quality_notes.all: Verify all materials match spec. Confirm anti-slip aggregate type. Stage in shade.

tasks.name: Porch Furniture & Obstacle Removal
tasks.description: Remove all furniture, planters, grills, rugs, doormats from porch surface. Stage in garage or yard. Document pre-existing surface condition. Photograph before clearing.

quality_notes.all: Photograph surface before clearing. Document all pre-existing damage. Get owner acknowledgment for unmovable items.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Mobilize first, then clear furniture. Surface must be fully accessible before protection or assessment.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor RP — Perimeter Protection
sop_modules.description: Mask all adjacent surfaces: wall-floor junction, railing post bases, door thresholds, landscape edges, hardscape transitions.

tasks.name: Wall-Floor Junction Masking
tasks.description: Apply masking tape and 6" paper at wall-to-floor junction along full perimeter. Exterior-grade tape rated 7+ day adhesion.

quality_notes.all: Tape tight to floor surface to prevent wicking. 6" paper minimum.

tasks.name: Railing Post Base Masking
tasks.description: Tape and mask railing post bases where posts meet porch floor. Paper collar around each post to prevent coating contact with railing finish.

quality_notes.all: Wrap tape fully around each post base. No gaps.

tasks.name: Door Threshold Masking
tasks.description: Mask door thresholds at porch-to-interior transitions. Tape along threshold edge, paper/plastic over threshold surface. Per door count.

quality_notes.all: Critical masking point — high visibility. Tape must be crisp.

tasks.name: Landscape Edge Protection
tasks.description: Deploy drop cloth along porch perimeter where landscape beds are adjacent. Protect plantings from scraping debris and coating splash.

quality_notes.all: Extend plastic 3-4 ft from porch edge for scraping debris containment.

tasks.name: Hardscape Edge Protection
tasks.description: Tape and drop cloth at hardscape transitions (driveway, sidewalk, adjacent patio). Prevent coating contact.

quality_notes.all: Tape at transition line for clean edge. Canvas for traffic areas.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Wall base first, railing bases, thresholds, landscape, hardscape. Work from structure outward.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor RP — Condition Assessment
sop_modules.description: RP-SPECIFIC: Assess existing coating condition, identify coating type, moisture check (concrete peeling), verify wood MC. Assessment drives all downstream prep and primer decisions.

tasks.name: Existing Coating Condition Assessment
tasks.description: Walk entire porch floor surface. Rate existing coating condition: sound (intact, good adhesion), worn (traffic wear-through in paths), failing (flaking/adhesion loss in patches), peeling (sheet delamination). Document per-area condition with photographs. Mark failing/peeling zones with chalk for scraping crew.

quality_notes.all: Tape-pull adhesion test at 3+ locations. Putty knife scratch test at wear areas. Photo-document all condition zones.

tasks.name: Existing Coating Type Identification
tasks.description: Identify existing coating type: porch enamel (most common), concrete stain, acrylic sealer, polyurea/epoxy (excluded from RP — flag for specialty), or unknown. Solvent wipe test and fingernail scratch test. Unknown triggers bonding primer requirement.

quality_notes.all: If polyurea/epoxy identified, STOP — outside standard RP scope. Unknown = treat as incompatible.

tasks.name: Concrete Moisture Assessment (Peeling Trigger)
tasks.description: When peeling pattern on concrete suggests moisture migration from below: perform plastic sheet test (ASTM D4263) or calcium chloride MVER test. If moisture detected, flag as root cause — repainting over active moisture will fail again. Recommend drainage/ventilation correction before repainting.

hard_stop.action: STOP — address moisture source before repainting
hard_stop.description: Coating applied over active moisture will delaminate again. Root cause must be corrected.

quality_notes.all: Document moisture test results. If positive, write scope limitation note for customer.

tasks.name: Wood Moisture Content Verification
tasks.description: Pin-type moisture meter test on wood porch floor substrate. MC must be <15% before coating. Test at minimum 3 locations including areas near planters, downspouts, and low-drainage spots.

hard_stop.description: Porch enamel over wet wood will blister and peel. Wait for MC <15%.

quality_notes.all: Document MC readings at all test points. Photo-document meter display.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Condition assessment first (drives everything), then coating ID, then substrate-specific moisture/MC checks.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor RP — Concrete Prep
sop_modules.description: Concrete-specific prep: chemical degloss or floor buffer for sound/worn, scrape + feather sand for failing/peeling, crack fill, clean. NO acid etch on RP.

tasks.name: Chemical Degloss — Concrete (Sound/Worn)
tasks.description: Apply liquid sander/deglosser to sound or worn existing porch enamel on concrete. Wipe on with mop or pad, allow dwell time per product instructions. Dulls glossy surface for adhesion without mechanical sanding. Alternative: floor buffer with abrasive pad.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage — no puddles. Ventilate area. Rinse residue before coating.

tasks.name: Scrape Loose/Failing Paint — Concrete
tasks.description: Scrape all loose, flaking, and delaminating paint from concrete surface using 4" scraper and/or floor scraper. Remove all material that does not pass tape-pull adhesion test. Collect scraping debris for disposal.

quality_notes.all: All loose material removed. No coating lifts when scraped with putty knife. Collect and bag all debris.

tasks.name: Feather-Edge Sand Scrape Boundaries — Concrete
tasks.description: Sand transition zones where scraped bare concrete meets intact existing coating. 80-grit to feather edges smooth — no sharp step between bare and coated areas. This is critical for smooth finish appearance.

quality_notes.all: No visible edge step at scrape boundaries. Smooth transition from bare to coated.

tasks.name: Concrete Crack Fill
tasks.description: Fill hairline to 1/4" cracks with flexible concrete patching compound. Cracks >1/4" are outside painting scope — flag for concrete repair. Allow patch to cure per manufacturer TDS before priming.

quality_notes.all: Patch flush with surrounding surface. Cracks >1/4" documented and excluded.

tasks.name: Clean Concrete Surface — Dust & Debris Removal
tasks.description: Sweep and vacuum all sanding dust, scraping debris, and loose material from concrete surface. Final wipe with damp mop. Surface must be clean and dry before prime/coat.

quality_notes.all: No visible dust, debris, or loose particles. Surface dry to touch before coating.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Degloss OR scrape (condition-dependent) -> feather sand -> crack fill -> clean. Always end with clean surface.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor RP — Wood Prep
sop_modules.description: Wood-specific prep: scuff sand for sound/worn, scrape + feather sand for failing/peeling, T&G joint cleanup, dust removal.

tasks.name: Scuff Sand Existing Coating — Wood (Sound/Worn)
tasks.description: Light scuff sand existing porch enamel with 120-150 grit to degloss and promote adhesion. Use orbital sander or sanding block for field areas. Hand-sand T&G joint grooves with folded sandpaper.

quality_notes.all: Uniform dull sheen across entire surface. No skipped areas. T&G grooves sanded.

tasks.name: Scrape Loose/Failing Paint — Wood
tasks.description: Scrape all loose, flaking paint from wood porch surface. Use 4" scraper for flat areas, detail scraper for T&G grooves. Remove all material failing tape-pull test.

quality_notes.all: All loose material removed. Extra attention to T&G joints where moisture enters.

tasks.name: Feather-Edge Sand Scrape Boundaries — Wood
tasks.description: Sand transition zones between scraped bare wood and intact existing coating. 80-grit for feathering, 120-grit for smoothing. Critical for professional-grade finish.

quality_notes.all: No visible edge step. Smooth transition. All sanding dust cleaned before prime.

tasks.name: Wood Filler — T&G Gaps and Surface Damage
tasks.description: Fill open T&G joints, nail holes, and minor surface damage with exterior wood filler. Allow to cure, sand flush. Conditional on damage presence.

quality_notes.all: Fill flush with surrounding surface. Do not overfill T&G joints — allow for expansion.

tasks.name: Clean Wood Surface — Dust & Debris Removal
tasks.description: Sweep, vacuum, and tack-cloth all sanding dust and scraping debris from wood surface. All T&G grooves cleaned of debris.

quality_notes.all: No visible dust or debris. T&G grooves clean. Surface dry.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Scuff sand OR scrape (condition-dependent) -> feather sand -> fill -> clean. Always end clean.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor RP — Primer Application
sop_modules.description: Condition-driven primer: spot prime bare areas (failing), full prime (peeling), bonding primer (incompatible coating). Not needed on sound/worn with intact existing coating.

tasks.name: Spot Prime Bare Areas — Roller
tasks.description: Roll primer on all bare substrate areas exposed by scraping. On concrete: acrylic exterior primer on bare concrete patches. On wood: acrylic exterior primer on bare wood. Coverage is effective SF of bare area, not total floor SF.

quality_notes.all: Full hide on all bare substrate. Feathered edges where primer meets existing coating. Brush primer into T&G joints on wood.

tasks.name: Full Prime Coat — Roller
tasks.description: Roll full prime coat over entire floor surface. Required when peeling condition exposes >30% bare substrate. Full-coverage primer application.

quality_notes.all: Full, even coverage. No holidays. Brush edges and T&G joints.

tasks.name: Bonding Primer — Full Coat (Incompatible Existing)
tasks.description: Apply bonding primer (Stix or equivalent) over entire floor surface when existing coating is unknown or incompatible (e.g., concrete stain, acrylic sealer remnants). Provides adhesion bridge for porch enamel.

quality_notes.all: Full coverage mandatory. Do not spot-apply bonding primer — entire surface needs adhesion bridge.

tasks.name: Prime Steps — Brush (Spot or Full)
tasks.description: Brush-apply primer on step treads and risers. Spot or full coverage matching field prime scope. Alternating-step pattern for access.

quality_notes.all: Full coverage on treads and risers. Step nosing fully coated.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Spot OR full prime (condition-dependent), then bonding prime (coating-type-dependent), then steps. Only one prime path active per project.

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor RP — Porch Enamel Application
sop_modules.description: Apply porch & floor enamel: coat 1 with anti-slip broadcast, coat 2 smooth. Field by roll or spray_backroll, edges by brush, steps by brush.

tasks.name: Cut-In Edges — Brush (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Brush-cut all edges: wall base, railing bases, threshold transitions, expansion joints, and T&G joint back-brush on wood. Cut-in before field rolling.

quality_notes.all: Clean tape line at thresholds. Brush into all T&G joints on wood. No drips at railing bases.

tasks.name: Porch Enamel — Field Roll (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Roll porch & floor enamel on floor field area using 18" roller with 3/8" or 1/2" nap cover. Work from far end toward exit. Maintain wet edge. Even film build for anti-slip aggregate embedment.

quality_notes.all: Even film build. No holidays, runs, or puddles. Work toward exit point.

tasks.name: Porch Enamel — Spray + Backroll (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Spray porch enamel with airless sprayer, immediately backroll with 18" roller. 2-person crew: one sprays, one backrolls. Spray provides speed, backroll ensures film build and texture uniformity.

quality_notes.all: Uniform spray pattern. Backroll within 30 seconds of spray pass. No dry spots.

tasks.name: Anti-Slip Aggregate Broadcast — Field
tasks.description: Broadcast silica sand anti-slip aggregate into wet coat 1 before it skins over. Even distribution — approximately 1 lb per 100 SF. Broadcast by hand-throwing or shaker can. Must be done immediately after rolling/spraying while coating is wet.

quality_notes.all: Even distribution. No clumps. No bare patches. Must complete before coating skins (~15-20 min).

tasks.name: Steps — Porch Enamel Coat 1 (Brush)
tasks.description: Brush-apply porch enamel coat 1 on step treads and risers. Alternating-step pattern: paint odd steps, allow to set, paint even steps. Anti-slip aluminum oxide broadcast on treads immediately.

quality_notes.all: Alternating pattern for access. Aluminum oxide on treads. Full riser coverage.

tasks.name: Cut-In Edges — Brush (Coat 2)
tasks.description: Repeat edge cut-in for coat 2. Same perimeter as coat 1.

quality_notes.all: Match coat 1 cut-in lines. Full hide on edges.

tasks.name: Porch Enamel — Field Roll (Coat 2)
tasks.description: Roll coat 2 over anti-slip aggregate from coat 1. Encapsulates aggregate and builds final film. Smooth, even application.

quality_notes.all: Coat 2 encapsulates aggregate. Even film. No roller marks.

tasks.name: Porch Enamel — Spray + Backroll (Coat 2)
tasks.description: Spray + backroll coat 2 over anti-slip aggregate from coat 1. Same 2-person crew method as coat 1.

quality_notes.all: Encapsulate aggregate evenly. No dry spray. Backroll immediately.

tasks.name: Steps — Porch Enamel Coat 2 (Brush)
tasks.description: Brush-apply coat 2 on step treads and risers. Alternating-step pattern. Encapsulates aluminum oxide aggregate from coat 1.

quality_notes.all: Coat 2 over aggregate. Full coverage on treads and risers.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Cut-in edges -> field roll/spray -> anti-slip broadcast (coat 1) -> steps coat 1 -> dry time (4-24 hr) -> cut-in coat 2 -> field coat 2 -> steps coat 2. QT2 = 1 coat only (no coat 2 tasks).

sop_modules.name: Porch Floor RP — Inspection, Teardown & Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Final inspection, touch-up, protection removal, furniture return, tool cleanup, and customer cure-time communication.

tasks.name: Final Inspection & Touch-Up
tasks.description: Walk entire floor surface. Check for holidays, thin spots, roller marks, missed edges, threshold tape line quality. Touch-up with brush as needed. Verify anti-slip texture uniformity.

quality_notes.all: No holidays. Anti-slip aggregate visible and uniform. Tape lines clean. Steps fully covered.

tasks.name: Protection Removal & Teardown
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape, paper, plastic, and drop cloths. Pull tape while coating is still slightly tacky for cleanest edge (within 2-4 hours of final coat). Inspect all protected surfaces for coating contact.

quality_notes.all: Pull tape at 45-degree angle. Check all protected surfaces for overspray/contact. Clean any spots immediately.

tasks.name: Furniture Return (After Cure)
tasks.description: Return porch furniture to original positions. NOTE: furniture return is scheduled AFTER 48-72 hour foot traffic cure. Light foot traffic at 24 hours. Heavy furniture at 7 days. This task may be a return visit.

quality_notes.all: Use felt pads under furniture legs. Do not drag — lift and place. Verify floor surface intact under furniture placement.

tasks.name: Customer Cure-Time Communication
tasks.description: Inform customer of cure schedule: light foot traffic 24 hours, normal foot traffic 48-72 hours, heavy furniture 7 days. Advise alternate entry path during cure period if porch is primary entrance. Leave written cure schedule.

quality_notes.all: Written cure schedule provided. Alternate entry path confirmed. Customer acknowledges.

tasks.name: Tool & Equipment Cleanup
tasks.description: Clean rollers, brushes, spray equipment (if used), scrapers. Properly dispose of scraping debris. Pack and load equipment.

quality_notes.all: All tools cleaned. Scraping debris bagged and removed. No equipment left on site.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect -> remove protection -> customer communication -> tool cleanup. Furniture return is separate visit after cure.
